transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I've been having these episodes where I eat a lot, and afterward, I just feel so gross. I get really disappointed in myself. It feels like I should have more control, you know? And then I end up writing awful things about myself in my journal. It's just getting to be too much.
During these episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah, I do. Like, on some nights after my cleaning shift, I’ll stop at the convenience store just meaning to grab a normal dinner. But I end up getting a big bowl of ramen, several rice balls, fried chicken, and a bunch of sweets. And then I take it all back to my room and eat everything in... maybe an hour or two.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don't do that. I just... I sit there feeling really full and miserable, but I've never tried to make myself throw up or anything. I just let it pass.
After you overeat, do you ever try to make up for it by fasting, exercising a lot, or using laxatives or diuretics?

No, I don't really do any of that either. I mean, I don't take laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise a lot... my job keeps me on my feet all day, so when I get home, I'm just tired. I don't really fast, either. I usually just wake up the next day feeling awful about myself and try to eat normally, but then it just happens again eventually.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel like you can’t stop eating or control what or how much you’re eating?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... once I start, I just keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. Even while I'm sitting there thinking to myself, 'Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,' I don't actually stop. I just keep going until all the food is gone, or until I feel too uncomfortable to eat another bite.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yeah, they do. I mean, like I said before, I feel pretty awful about myself afterwards. It's just really frustrating to feel like I don't have control over it. I don't know if I'd call it severe distress or anything, since I still get up and go to work and everything, but it definitely upsets me and makes me feel really down.
